results.reasoning: Judged in four throwaway projects, each with its own HOME, never against the real ledger. Provenance, the half that was failing: in the default layout (code in git, home in ~/.walkdown) a checks run now records the CODE repository's sha with -dirty and a tree_hash; with the home kept in git at its own commit, a sweep, two checks runs (one driven from an unrelated cwd with --project) and a walkdown filed through the running panel's POST /api/walkdowns all carry the code repository's sha and never the home's; the committed layout records it too (provenance-after-fix.txt, probes A-C). The one shape that still records nothing is an --ephemeral copy standing outside any repository with no roots declared - there the writer refuses to stamp the repository you happen to be standing in, which is the right refusal, though `walkdown where code` still names that repository, so the report and the record disagree in that one shape; nothing misdirects, so I did not fail on it. Currency, the half that already held, holds under harder pressure: two unrelated commits, a branch and a --no-ff merge, an untracked file, and then a history rewrite that made the recorded sha unresolvable left `status --json`, the human table and every run file byte-identical, while a statement reword and a sweep each moved exactly that one cell (currency-holds.txt). docs/05-runs-ledger.md no longer claims an older git_sha renders stale.
